clue.text: Meeting record takes order for food

indicators.note: to order something is to arrange it, so the preceding word is put into a new sequence

blocks.note: the written record of a meeting is its minutes
the letters of takes, rearranged

explanation.surface: A secretary noting down the lunch order during a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Takes looks like the verb joining record to order, but it is the anagram fodder, and the word break falls one letter earlier than the wordplay's.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute steaks are thin cuts of beef cooked very quickly, a dish one can eat.

clue.text: Wine and cheese served up by republicans

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned around

blocks.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese
the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: Wine and cheese being offered at a republican gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of that name.

clue.text: Group problem playing tennis?

blocks.note: surface reading: a difficulty that might arise during a game of tennis
setter's reading: the problem is that the court lacks the thing players hit over

explanation.surface: A group of players having trouble during their tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words, no + net, and you have the tennis problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians, or a piece written for them.

clue.text: Port, originally in Libya, is needing renovation

definitions.text: Port, originally in Libya, is needing renovation

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the start of each following word is used
something needing renovation must be rebuilt, so the letters are remade into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
first letters of in, Libya and is

explanation.surface: A Libyan port that is badly in need of rebuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer, while its words also supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya and a seaport on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: See 1
A term composition to include piano and fiddle

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are assembled in a new order
including something means taking it inside, so one letter goes within the others

blocks.note: the letters of a term, rearranged
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A music student's termly composition including parts for piano and fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like the violin, alongside the piano, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle with something is to interfere with it, which is to tamper.

clue.text: George’s dysfunctional utopia followed by many

indicators.note: a dysfunctional thing is not working properly, so the word's letters are disordered

blocks.note: the letters of utopia, rearranged
a lot means many

explanation.surface: A man called George whose ideal world turns out badly, imitated by crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: George is old slang, from pilots, for an aircraft's automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircrew traditionally nicknamed the automatic flight-control system George, so the name stands for the device.

clue.text: Rush to contain firm’s misfortune

indicators.note: to contain something is to hold it within, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: a surge is a sudden rush
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company has a sudden rush of bad luck that must be contained.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a cause of great suffering or affliction, a source of calamity.

clue.text: Paint technique can feature in fraud

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: a sting is a confidence trick
the tab on a drink can that you pull to open it

explanation.surface: A painting method that might appear in an art forgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paint technique' suggests brushwork, but string pulling is also an art method: paint-soaked string drawn between paper. A ring pull is the tab on a drink can.
explanation.definitionFit: String pulling is a decorative art method where paint-soaked twine is pulled from folded paper to leave patterns.

clue.text: Prime minister’s garden

blocks.note: first meaning: Sir Anthony ..., British prime minister 1955-57
second meaning: the biblical garden of Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: A prime minister's private garden at his residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Eden was the Conservative prime minister at the time of the Suez crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a postwar British premier and to the paradise in Genesis where humanity began.

clue.text: Suggestion of heartless bullying

indicators.note: without a heart, the word that follows loses its central letters

blocks.note: bullying someone into compliance is intimidation

explanation.surface: A hint that a heartless person has been bullying others.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve-letter word has ID at its centre; take those two out.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimation is a hint or indirect suggestion of something, conveyed without stating it outright.

clue.text: Travelling Brits love a French eatery

indicators.note: things travelling move about, so the following word's letters move into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of Brits, rearranged
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: British tourists abroad fall for a little French restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant of the kind associated with France, serving simple food.

clue.text: One each afterwards held as unskilled

indicators.note: something held is gripped inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
what comes next comes afterwards
as in so much per head, meaning each

explanation.surface: Someone taken on, one at a time, and then kept on despite being unskilled.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the pieces out of order: the each piece sits inside the afterwards piece, with the one at the very front.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpert means lacking skill or expertise, an exact synonym for being untrained or clumsy.

clue.text: Perhaps I’m grabbed, grabbed by hint of colour

indicators.note: perhaps signals one possible arrangement, so the next words' letters may be reordered
being grabbed by something means being clutched inside it

blocks.note: a hint is a clue
the letters of I'm grabbed, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they have been seized, then are grabbed by a mere trace of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hint of colour' looks like a first-letter instruction, but hint is the word CLUE and colour is the definition. The repeated 'grabbed' serves twice: once as fodder, once as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge blue is a pale greenish-blue shade, the sporting colour of Cambridge University.

clue.text: Celebrity starts to eat dinner, with bubbles

indicators.note: the starts are the opening letters of each of the following words

blocks.note: a B-lister is a minor celebrity
first letters of eat and dinner

explanation.surface: A celebrity starts on dinner, accompanied by champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With bubbles' suggests champagne but defines skin covered in raised blisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blistered skin or paint is covered in raised swellings, small domes like bubbles.

clue.text: See 13
Armenians oddly out of control

indicators.note: oddly here means taking out the odd letters, so only the even-placed ones are kept

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Armenians behaving strangely and getting out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of control' is read as a phrase in reverse: to rein something in is to control it, and 'rein' is what control is out of.
explanation.definitionFit: Control and restraint over a horse comes from the rein, so free rein means the absence of control; the noun stands for control itself.

clue.text: City needs diplomacy to make an undiplomatic declaration

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city
tact is diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: A city's diplomats are told they must make a blunt statement.
explanation.walkthrough: The word break in the answer falls one letter before the join between city and diplomacy. Reading the riot act was originally a formal order to disperse a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading someone the riot act means giving a stern, forceful reprimand, far from tactful.

clue.text: How to remove plaster and succeed

blocks.note: first meaning: the literal instruction for taking off a sticking plaster
second meaning: the idiom for managing something difficult

explanation.surface: Advice for removing a sticking plaster and managing it successfully.
explanation.walkthrough: A plaster here is a sticking plaster, the British name for an adhesive bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage a difficult feat is the idiom; literally the phrase describes yanking an adhesive bandage away.

clue.text: One benefits from entry in shelter

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A person who profits from getting into a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One benefits' is a noun phrase: one who benefits, a beneficiary.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee inherits a bequest under a will, so is someone who gains from it.

clue.text: Florida’s capital not just an amusement park

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter
not just means unfair

explanation.surface: Florida's capital city is more than simply a theme park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not just' looks like 'not merely', but it means unjust.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair is a travelling fair with rides and stalls, a temporary pleasure ground.

clue.text: Dog breeder’s primary advantage

indicators.note: primary means first, so the word's leading letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter
an asset is an advantage

explanation.surface: A dog breeder's chief selling point.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hound with long ears, a breed of hunting canine.

clue.text: Ballot of sporting venue?

blocks.note: these letters, when rearranged, spell the first word of the entry
the question mark flags a reverse clue: the entry's second word is the missing anagram signal, meaning crushed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A vote taken among supporters about a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the entry is itself the wordplay. Read the answer as an instruction, the first word ground up, meaning crushed into a new shape, and it yields 'Ballot of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A football ground is a stadium where the game is played, an obvious kind of place for sport.

clue.text: See 21
Decimal, many times

blocks.note: decimal describes counting in tens; split the letters as a two-word phrase

explanation.surface: Decimal arithmetic, practised again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Decimal comes from the Latin for tenth, so a decimal system is one of ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, on numerous occasions.

clue.text: Revered like this clue, promoting the end can’t change

indicators.note: promoting the end lifts the final letter up to the front of the preceding word
to change something is to alter it, so the letters of the preceding word get altered in order

blocks.note: this clue runs across the grid
the letters of can't, rearranged

explanation.surface: Something so revered that it cannot be altered, ends included.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the last S of ACROSS to its front gives SACROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrosanct means too sacred or important to be interfered with, so regarded with reverence.

clue.text: Backing of shops for public transport

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: a mart is a market or shop

explanation.surface: Financial support from retailers for buses and trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger vehicle on street rails, one form of transport open to everyone.

clue.text: Gallery has welcomed reactionary party till now

indicators.note: a reactionary wants to go back, so the word is turned backwards
welcoming someone takes them inside, so one word is put within another

blocks.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: An art gallery hosted a political party of reactionaries, and still does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reactionary party' looks like a political group, but party is just DO, reversed. The Tate is a national gallery group in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something achieved so far, up to the present moment, is achieved up until this point.

clue.text: Having lost weight, student lost heart

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letter of the word goes

blocks.note: a learner is a student

explanation.surface: A student who slimmed down and became discouraged along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thinner after a diet means having less fat, so someone slimmer than before.
